evidence_quotes.agenda: 'Let's talk about your move. What are your biggest concerns and what are the most important things you want answers during this call today?' — asked right after the date, before any logistics probing (full 10pts)
evidence_quotes.two_layers_deep: Customer answered with real concerns — 'my standing desk, we have an electronic piano that's pretty heavy... mirrors and things like that, TVs' — but Jules only said 'sounds good' and pivoted straight to collecting name/email, never circling back to dig into or reassure on the fragile/heavy-item worry (0pts)
evidence_quotes.save_your_ass: 'it took us like the minimum, you'll only pay for the minimum' tied to the actual-time billing explanation (beats-it-pay-less, 3pts) + 'depends on how much disassembly and reassembly needed and the traffic as well' (window framing, 3pts); no rate-commit, no prep tip, no 'does that feel fair'

top_strength: Textbook agenda-question placement — asked cleanly before any probing began — and a well-personalized 3-5 hour range with concrete cost examples for a partial-inventory move.
coaching_note: This is the CET agenda-opener failure mode by the book: asked the line, got real concerns back (heavy piano, large mirrors, desk), and did nothing with them — no two-layer follow-up, and never answered with the damage-coverage/'we move it like it's ours' line even though the customer as good as asked for it.
